text:
lina: Thinking out loud — propose a "progressive_shift" policy for canaries that supports weighted decay + explicit rollback hooks. Want the gateway to automatically reduce weight on adverse signals and call a rollback webhook if thresholds are hit.

sanjay: +1 on automation. What signals are we monitoring? error_rate, p99, and business metrics?

jordan: Core signals: `error_rate` (5xx), `p99_latency`, `user_quality_regressions` (from eval service). Also token_cost per-request for cost guardrails.

lina: Yup. Sketch of config (pseudo-yaml):
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
match: { path_prefix: "/v1", header: { "x-experiment": "canary-42" } }
policy:
  type: progressive_shift
  initial_weight: 0.1
  max_weight: 0.5
  step: 0.1
  step_interval: 15m
  decay_on_signal: true
  decay_factor: 0.5
  signals:
    - name: error_rate
      window: 5m
      threshold: 0.02
    - name: p99_latency
      window: 10m
      threshold_ms: 1500
  rollback_hook: "https://ops.internal/rollbacks/canary-42"
  sampling_key: "customer_id_or_cookie"
```

maya: Love the config. Can we make `sampling_key` optional and default to prefix hashing if not set? Some teams don't have cookies. :thinking_face: 

jordan: Also need header override precedence rules. If a client sets `x-routing-override: full`, should that bypass progressive_shift? I think yes for internal testing, but we must rate-limit overrides.

lina: Agree. Proposed precedence: explicit `x-routing-override` (only from allowlist) -> route-level policy -> org/global defaults. We'll add `override_allowlist` and `override_quota` to policy schema.

sanjay: Telemetry: tag metrics with `canary_id`, `slice` (A/B), and `sampling_key` hash. Dashboard should show comparison cohort side-by-side and rolling risk score. Can we make the rollout UI show both signal deltas and a projected cost delta?

dev-ex: UX notes: show a timeline control to manually advance steps, plus an auto-mode with pause-on-signal. Provide a one-click rollback that triggers the rollback_hook and sets weight to 0. Also show recent users exposed (scrubbed) and a link to the eval prompt set.

maya: Security question — rollback_hook externally callable? That URL needs mTLS and an execution token, otherwise team could spoof. ops-bot: Initiating canary run for /v1/generate (canary-42) at 1767801300 :rocket:

lina: Good call. Rollback hook must require signed JWT from gateway and be per-tenant. We'll add `rollback_auth` fields: `mode: mtls|jwt` and `audience`.

jordan: Edge case: weighted decay could oscillate if signal is noisy. Suggest add hysteresis: require consecutive windows failing before decay/rollback, and a cooldown after a rollback.

sanjay: Also we should expose a `simulated_traffic` API so QA can run parallel and estimate impacts without billing real customers. That helps QA A/B evaluation.

maya: About quotas — if the canary is high-cost model, we must enforce quota at routing layer, not just at metering. Otherwise cost spikes bypass budget. Add `quota_policy` with `hard_limit` and `grace_window`.

lina: Action items: 1) draft full OpenAPI for policy CRD with fields we discussed (lina) 2) telemetry contract for metric tags + hysteresis logic (sanjay) 3) UI mockups for progressive_shift controls + rollback button (dev-ex) 4) security design for rollback hooks (maya) 5) decide header override semantics and allowlist management (jordan).

jordan: I'm happy to take header/allowlist.

maya: I'll take rollback auth and quota bits.

ops-bot: @lina scheduled a follow-up sync: #eng-platform canary-policy review — 1767802000 :calendar: 

lina: Thanks all. If no objections I'll open an RFC and add the YAML example to the repo. :thumbsup:
